narrative.overview: The site reads like a well-kept engineering notebook left open on a desk: cool paper, navy ink, one blue pen, and annotations in the margin. Every page is a dated record of work rather than a pitch. The hero lays the name out at poster scale over a faint blueprint grid; the build log runs down a ruled spine with sticky years; project cards are numbered plates with category-tinted fields. Nothing is illustrated for its own sake. The grid, the rule and the index number do the decorating. The voice of the interface matches the voice of the writing: plain, specific, quietly confident. Inter carries every headline and paragraph at editorial sizes, with negative tracking that makes large type feel drawn rather than set. JetBrains Mono appears only where a record-keeping device would put it: entry indices, counts, dates, category labels, small metadata. The result should feel precise and slightly technical without ever becoming a dashboard. Density is generous but not luxurious. Sections breathe at 72–120px, two-column splits are deliberately asymmetric, and prose is held to 46–68 characters per line. Depth comes from tonal panels and one-pixel hairlines; shadows are reserved for contact (hover), overlays and the sticky nav. Motion is a short lift, an arrow nudge, a marquee that pauses when read. The work is the evidence; the interface stays out of its way.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper and navy ink, with a single Signal Blue accent at roughly 10% of any screen.
Asymmetric editorial grids: 1.3/0.7 hero, 1.18/0.62 about, ruled three-track build log.
One-pixel hairlines and pale tonal panels instead of borders, cards-on-cards or heavy chrome.
Inter for reading, JetBrains Mono for annotation; no second display face.
Category colour (cyan, amber, violet) reserved for discipline coding, never for mood.
Flat at rest, lifted on contact; no decorative shadows.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only colour allowed to mean "do this". Keep it under roughly 10% of any screen; its rarity is what makes it read as authorship.

rules.name: The Discipline, Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Cyan, amber and violet encode project category. Never use them for generic emphasis, hover states, or section variety. The App category reuses Signal Blue.

rules.name: The Paper-First Rule
rules.body: Every colour decision must survive both themes with the same hierarchy. Never introduce a colour that only works on white or only on navy.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Inter sets every sentence and every headline. Do not introduce a serif, a geometric display face, or a second sans to create contrast; create it with weight, size and tracking.

rules.name: The Tight Headline Rule
rules.body: Anything at 34px or larger takes negative tracking between -0.025em and -0.06em. Body copy never takes negative tracking.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Mono is a record-keeping device, not a style. If a string is not an index, count, date, category or technical tag, set it in Inter.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Contact Rule
rules.body: A surface may move only when the pointer or keyboard is on it. No card floats at rest, and no shadow is used to fill empty space.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: When two surfaces need separating, try a 1px line and a tonal step before a shadow. If a shadow is doing structural work, the layout is wrong.

rules.name: The Pills-Are-Labels Rule
rules.body: Full-round shapes only mark a label or a filter. Primary buttons, cards and inputs are never pills.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: A surface uses one radius, not nested radii. If a card is 16px, its cover and inner blocks clip to the card, they do not add their own.

dos: Do keep Signal Blue for action and authorship only, and hold it to roughly 10% of the viewport.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px Hairline and a tonal step before reaching for a shadow.
Do set indices, counts, dates and category labels in JetBrains Mono at 11px uppercase; 9–10px belongs only to inherited micro-meta.
Do give anything above 34px negative tracking (-0.025em to -0.06em) and leave body copy at 0.
Do use 16px for cards, 24px for large panels, 10px for small entries, and 999px only for labels.
Do keep the 2px accent focus ring with 3px offset visible in both themes.
Do let category colour live in dots, cover tints and ghost numerals, at low opacity.
Do preserve the reduced-motion fallback: no marquee, no reveal transform, no scroll animation.
donts: Don't use cyan, amber or violet as generic accents; they are category codes.
Don't add resting shadows to cards, sections or panels.
Don't introduce a second typeface for display, quotes or "personality".
Don't set long labels or sentences in mono, or uppercase Inter paragraphs.
Don't make primary buttons or cards into pills.
Don't nest radii: a card clips its cover and inner blocks to its own 16px corner.
Don't stack cards inside cards or add decorative gradients outside cover plates and the ambient washes.
Don't invent metrics, logos or screenshots to fill a layout; an empty slot stays empty.
